issues.description: The task specifies input as a string and does not define behavior for None; the code returns False for None. This is a reasonable defensive choice but is an unrequested extension of the contract.
issues.suggestion: Optionally document the None behavior in the task contract or remove the None guard so the function only handles strings as specified.

summary: The implementation correctly uses a stack to scan the string once, pushing '(', '[', '{' and validating closing brackets against the top of the stack, returning False on mismatched or unmatched closers and True only when the stack is empty at the end. Empty strings and bracket-free strings return True, other characters are ignored, and the function is pure with no printing, I/O, or external dependencies. The only minor note is the unrequested None guard, which does not violate any stated requirement.
